=== Goal ===
Objective: Deliver the full standalone big_cabinet PR established by the October 6–13 design transcript: highly usable, high-quality, comprehensively tested Cabinet components, without supplanting existing Daybook code, using concurrent GPT 5.6 Luna high workers for virtually all implementation and substantial qualification work.

Main tenet — preserve across compactions:
The original design transcript is the primary authority. Almost every genuine design question has already been discussed there. When uncertain, consult the transcript first, including its compaction digests and relevant original turns; do not redesign from a recap or invent decisions. When the transcript does not answer a question, inspect daybook_core and higher-layer usage of the components being replaced to understand real consumer needs. Existing usage guides usability, not preservation of old implementation defects. Keep this rule, authoritative source locations, decisions, and pending deliverables explicit in the tracking document and every continuation/compaction handoff.

Success criteria:
- Establish an exhaustive, source-backed inventory of all PR deliverables, dependencies, existing implementations, remaining gaps, deferrals, and tailored acceptance gates before substantial feature work.
- Deliver the in-scope facet/schema authoring, canonical codecs and reconciliation, compatibility checking and schema registration, cleaned facet indexes, documents and branching, drawers and child drawers, authority/actors/capabilities, shared service infrastructure, typed clients, agreed transport contracts/adapters, interpreted projections, mutation receipts, observations, lifecycle, and documentation.
- Reorganize SampleRepo into shared service infrastructure and separate sample-specific modules, preserving the agreed semantics and providing a usable tested reference.
- Evaluate every component and boundary for practical consumer usability, correctness, performance, adherence to the transcript, and meaningful coverage. Working behavior is required wherever agreed scope requires it; placeholders, shallow tests, worker claims, and unimplemented seams cannot stand in for delivery.
- Maintain a dedicated subdocument containing every deliverable, source provenance, owner/workspace, dependencies, acceptance gates, exact verification evidence, findings, integration status, unresolved questions, and residual risks. Parent is personally accountable for the complete map and honest acceptance; all mandatory items must pass before completion.

Boundaries:
- This PR builds Cabinet alongside existing code. Do not supplant existing implementations or migrate daybook_core, daybook_types, runtime, plugs, or application consumers to Cabinet.
- Read daybook_core and above to validate intended workflows and ergonomics where transcript evidence is insufficient. Put representative consumer scenarios in Cabinet-local tests/examples without modifying those production consumers.
- Deliver big_cabinet, big_cabinet_core, and necessary supporting macros, shared service infrastructure, tests, and documentation according to transcript scope. Specific API details may be selected without reopening settled design, subject to consumer usability and agreed semantics.
- Preserve the existing Panproto POC. Panproto integration, upstream/Daybook integration, subsets, self-group drawers, roster sharding, recovery principals, and other explicitly deferred work stay out unless authoritative transcript evidence says otherwise.
- Current ADRs/FDRs, wiki documents, play.stack.md, the Cabinet task document, and review ledger support scope reconstruction; discrepancies must be reconciled against the transcript, not silently treated as new requirements.

Constraints:
- Target the user's 99.99% worker-execution division: GPT 5.6 Luna high workers perform virtually all code changes, fixes/greening, substantive reviews, test construction, test execution, and qualification. Parent is the map-owning orchestrator: scope reconstruction, bounded assignments, dependencies, concurrency, integration coordination, evidence scrutiny, acceptance decisions, and truthful tracking. Parent must avoid major implementation or qualification efforts rather than becoming a second feature worker.
- Discover and explicitly select the exact available GPT 5.6 Luna model with high thinking. Never silently use Sol or another model. Reuse eligible workers and use fresh-context Luna reviewers for independent acceptance rather than accepting implementation workers' self-reports.
- Prefer concurrent execution of independent bounded pieces to minimize wall-clock time, with one writer per workspace and explicit dependency barriers. Use jj workspaces for isolation when needed, never git commands, and follow governed delegation requirements. No silent protocol fallback on infrastructure failure.
- Configure isolated workspace build environments under .env with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/run/media/asdf/p3N/tmp/townframe-target or another appropriate p3N/tmp directory as explicitly authorized. Avoid conflicting concurrent builds. Monitor space; if p3N/tmp targets consume excessive space, instruct their owning workers to clean the appropriate target directories, coordinating with active builds and preserving non-build data.
- Follow AGENTS.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and relevant skills; preserve user work and the Panproto POC. Do not skip tests, conceal failures, use abstraction-breaking shims, or mark failures unrelated without pinning or instrumenting them.
- Every continuation must retain the transcript-first tenet, Luna-only execution contract, no-consumer-migration boundary, current inventory, exact worker identities/models, dependencies, verification evidence, blockers, and space/build ownership.

Verification contract:
- Each deliverable receives explicit, tailored acceptance gates before acceptance: design provenance, practical usability at its boundaries, correctness/performance review, and narrow meaningful tests. Property, snapshot, and deterministic simulation testing are available and should be used where they add real confidence, not mechanically or superficially.
- Luna implementation workers run narrow affected cargo-nextest tests, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features for affected crates, and formatting. Independent Luna reviewers inspect actual diffs and rerun targeted qualification; parent inspects evidence, resolves acceptance findings through workers, and refuses unsupported completion claims. Do not send bounded workers to run the full suite.
- Include Cabinet-local consumer-style and cross-component tests for authority, schema/storage semantics, heads-aware edits, branch/drawer behavior, source/projection ordering, read-after-event, completion receipts, transport ambiguity, cancellation, replay/live handoff, admission/backpressure, external changes, and shutdown where applicable.
- Conduct an integrated worker-led qualification and independent acceptance audit against the exhaustive inventory. Parent reconciles evidence and documentation, reports exact commands/results, and distinguishes implemented functionality from explicitly agreed deferred seams. Neither historical checks nor prior recap claims prove current acceptance.

If blocked: Consult the transcript first, then relevant existing consumer usage. Continue independent unblocked work and record the exact blocker and evidence. Ask the user only for a genuine unanswered product decision, irreconcilable source contradiction, explicit scope change, mandated-model substitution, or governed-protocol change. Do not invent decisions or claim completion while mandatory items remain blocked.
